imageHeadline: Bleeding on birth control doesn't mean you're pregnant
imageSubtext: What breakthrough bleeding actually means and when tests tell the truth
pinTitle: Abnormal Bleeding on Birth Control: When to Worry About Pregnancy
pinDescription: Breakthrough bleeding is one of the most common side effects of hormonal birth control, but it's easy to spiral when you've heard stories about hidden pregnancies. Learn what negative pregnancy tests actually mean, why bleeding happens months into your method, and when irregular bleeding needs medical follow-up.

items.label: Negative test + two methods = pregnancy very unlikely
Bleeding often continues past the 3-6 month window
Ultrasound can rule out structural causes like polyps
